findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancellation blocks all other cancellations
findings.body: All reminders are cancelled sequentially inside a single try block, while the Prisma delete operations are only executed by the Promise.all after the loop. If client.request throws for one reminder (for example an invalid, expired, or already-cancelled batch), the catch is taken, none of the queued deletes run, and every later reminder in remindersToCancel is never even attempted. The same failing reminder will be retried first on the next cron run, so other reminders whose scheduled time falls within the next hour can still be dispatched by SendGrid.

findings.title: Deferred-only cancellation misses reminders that are due imminently
findings.body: For a scheduled email this function now only sets cancelled=true and never cancels with SendGrid immediately, regardless of how soon the reminder is due. Cancellation therefore depends entirely on the periodic scheduleEmailReminders cron running before the SendGrid sendAt time. If a booking is cancelled a few minutes before its reminder and the next cron run happens after that time, SendGrid will already have sent the email; the cron's initial deleteMany for past scheduledDate rows then just removes the DB record. The previous immediate-cancellation behaviour covered this last-minute case.

findings.title: Reschedule path bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism and loses failures
findings.body: Rescheduling calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true), which immediately POSTs a SendGrid cancellation instead of setting cancelled=true. This reintroduces the exact SendGrid pending-cancellations cap (100) that this PR is meant to work around for rescheduled bookings. Worse, if that POST fails, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only logs the error and returns without deleting the row or setting cancelled, so the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only looks for cancelled=true) will never retry and the reminder for the old booking time will still be sent.

findings.title: Workflow deletion uses immediate cancellation then destroys the retry record
findings.body: Deleting a workflow calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true), which immediately cancels in SendGrid but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row; the code then deletes the workflow at line 220, and the WorkflowStep/WorkflowReminder cascade deletes the reminder rows. If the immediate SendGrid cancellation fails (including via the pending-cancellation cap described in the PR, or a transient error), the error is swallowed inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder and the DB record that the new cron-based deferred cancellation could have retried is gone, so the scheduled email will still be sent for a deleted workflow. The same pattern is used when a workflow step is deleted.

findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
findings.body: updatedBookings.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) / deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)) discards the promises returned by these async functions. The handler then awaits only unrelated attendee/reference deletions and returns a 200 response, so there is no guarantee the prisma update setting cancelled=true (or the SMS/Twilio cancellation and row deletion) has completed before the request finishes; in a serverless invocation the work can be cut short after the response, leaving cancelled=false in the database and allowing the cron/SendGrid schedule to send the reminder for the cancelled booking. The surrounding code cannot observe or retry the failure because the promise is dropped.
